# dlae2

> Computes the eigenvalues of a 2-by-2 symmetric matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlae2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlae2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlae2( a, b, c, rt1, rt2 ) → void
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `b` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,2) element (also (2,1)) of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `c` | `number` | in |  |  | (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `rt1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger absolute value |
| `rt2` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `b`: The (1,2) and (2,1) elements of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `c`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger absolute value.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlae2.ndarray( a, b, c, rt1, rt2 ) → void
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `b` | `number` | in |  |  | (1,2) element (also (2,1)) of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `c` | `number` | in |  |  | (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `rt1` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger absolute value |
| `rt2` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `b`: The (1,2) and (2,1) elements of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `c`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger absolute value.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlae2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAE2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlae2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable no-console */

import dlae2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlae2';

// Identity matrix — both eigenvalues are 1.0:
const rt1 = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rt2 = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlae2( 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, rt1, rt2 );
console.log( 'Identity: rt1=%d, rt2=%d', rt1[ 0 ], rt2[ 0 ] );

// Symmetric matrix with off-diagonal element:
dlae2( 2.0, 1.0, 2.0, rt1, rt2 );
console.log( 'Symmetric: rt1=%d, rt2=%d', rt1[ 0 ], rt2[ 0 ] );

// Negative trace (sm < 0):
dlae2( -3.0, 1.0, -5.0, rt1, rt2 );
console.log( 'Negative trace: rt1=%d, rt2=%d', rt1[ 0 ], rt2[ 0 ] );

// Zero trace (sm = 0, a = -c):
dlae2( 3.0, 2.0, -3.0, rt1, rt2 );
console.log( 'Zero trace: rt1=%d, rt2=%d', rt1[ 0 ], rt2[ 0 ] );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAE2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAE2 computes the eigenvalues of a 2-by-2 symmetric matrix

$$
\begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ B & C \end{bmatrix}
$$

On return, `RT1` is the eigenvalue of larger absolute value, and `RT2` is the eigenvalue of smaller absolute value.

### Further Details

`RT1` is accurate to a few ulps barring over/underflow.

`RT2` may be inaccurate if there is massive cancellation in the determinant $A \, C-B \, B$; higher precision or correctly rounded or correctly truncated arithmetic would be needed to compute `RT2` accurately in all cases.

Overflow is possible only if `RT1` is within a factor of 5 of overflow. Underflow is harmless if the input data is 0 or exceeds

underflow\_threshold / macheps.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
